quandoUsar: A password at login or password change, when the person wants to check what they typed before sending.
Other typed secrets, like an API key, by replacing the button names with `messages`.
quandoEvitar: Use `password-strength` when the person is creating a password and needs to see the requirements and strength while typing.

teclado.acao: Moves focus from the field to the eye button.
On the eye button, show or hide the password.

acessibilidade: `label` becomes a `<label>` tied to the field, and `description` goes into `aria-describedby` along with whatever you pass in that prop.
The eye button has `aria-pressed` and a name that toggles between `Show password` and `Hide password`; translate with `messages={{ showPassword, hidePassword }}`.
There is no error prop: pass `aria-invalid` for the border to turn red and tie your message via `aria-describedby`.
movimento: When showing the password, a stroke draws over the eye, cutting the outline from below, and retracts on hiding, instead of swapping one icon for the other.
The swap between dots and letters appears with a brief fade and blur from the first click, and the help line opens its own height with a spring.
With “reduce motion” on, the stroke swaps instantly, the text does not fade, and the button does not shrink when pressed.
notasIA: Accepts `<input>` props except `type` (`value`, `onChange`, `name`, `autoComplete`…) and the `ref` points to the field; use `autoComplete="current-password"` at login and `"new-password"` at signup.
Showing or hiding is internal state: there is no prop to control it or to know whether the password is visible.
